This pull request includes several changes to the project, focusing on adding automated tests, updating dependencies, and improving the API's CRUD operations. Here are the most important changes:

### Automated Tests

* Added a new GitHub Actions workflow to run unit tests on push events. This workflow sets up the environment, installs dependencies, and runs tests with coverage reporting. (`.github/workflows/test_on_push.yml`)

### Dependency Updates

* Updated the `.pre-commit-config.yaml` file to include `isort` for sorting imports and added arguments to `flake8` to ignore specific warnings. (`.pre-commit-config.yaml`)

### API Improvements

* Refactored the `api/crud.py` file to improve the CRUD operations, including the addition of a method to associate configuration files and updates to the `update_project` and `delete_project` methods for better handling of related entities. body:
This PR adds a napari-based alternative to the existing Neuroglancer precomputed mesh viewer. 

### Features
- Loads precomputed mesh data and displays each LOD (Level of Detail) as a separate layer in napari
- Uses the same directory validation logic as the original Neuroglancer viewer
- Visualizes each mesh fragment as a bounding box in 3D space
- Color-codes meshes by mesh ID for easy identification
- Follows the same UV-style command-line interface as the original: `uv run meshes/visualize-ng-precomputed/view_in_napari.py --mesh-dir precomputed`

### Implementation Details
- Reads and parses the binary `.index` files to understand the mesh structure
- Creates a simple proxy mesh visualization since full Draco decoding would require additional complexity
- Minimal dependencies: only requires napari, numpy and PyQt5

This provides a solution when the Neuroglancer viewer shows the "unsupported data source" error with "precomputed+file" sources.

body:
#### Summary
- Sends a user activity when a post contains a mention to the `@`username.
- Notification ends up in the activity on the teams application
- [x] Clicking on the activity in the list shows up Mattermost highlighting the message that triggered the activity.
- [x] Clicking on the desktop notification opens the tab application highlighting the message that triggered the activity.
- [x] Customize the notification (ex: `{user} mentioned you in Mattermost`)
- [x] Use a background runner to send the notifications
- [x] Icon in the activity list.

#### How this works

First we retrieve (along other params) the `app_id` in the authentication flow and store it in the user, since we need it to deeplink the "action" of the user activity notification (so we send the user to the tabApp or show the tabApp in the activities list, see screenshots).

The flow works this way:
- Using `MessageHasBeenPosted`, we check for the `@mention` in the message. **This don't work for keywords**, we would need to duplicate more code from server to make that work.
- If there's a mention and we have the attributes from the authentication stored for that user, we create a new UserActivity for the user in the Teams side, with a `post_(postid)` in the `context.subEntityId`. This context is sent to the tab application and we can retrieve it using `microsoftTeams.app.getContext()` (under `context.page.subPageId`).
- When the user lands in the `/iframe/authenticate`, we check if that value is set and get the necessary information to generate a `/(team)/pl/(post_id)` link to use as redirect url at the end of this handler. 
  - If the parameter is not set we redirect to `/` as usual.

#### Required permissions

1) Ensure `TeamsActivity.Send` is a granted permission under you application -> API permissions ([docs](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/teams-send-activityfeednotifications?tabs=desktop%2Chttp))

2) Ensure the `activities` section in the manifest is properly set:

```js
{
// ...
  "activities": {
    "activityTypes": [
      {
        "type": "mattermost_mention_with_name",
        "description": "New message in Mattermost for the Teams user",
        "templateText": "{post_author} mentioned you in Mattermost."
      }
    ]
  }
// ...
}
```

body:
## Description

Fixes the following warning during `dotnet pack`:
```
This project cannot be packaged because packaging has been disabled.
Add <IsPackable>true</IsPackable> to the project file to enable producing a package from this project.
```

The warning is caused by `Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web.ProjectSystem.props`:
```xml
<IsPackable Condition="'$(IsPackable)' == ''">false</IsPackable>
<WarnOnPackingNonPackableProject Condition="'$(WarnOnPackingNonPackableProject)' == '' and '$(IsPackable)' == 'false'">true</WarnOnPackingNonPackableProject>
```

which is imported by `<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web">` in the project file. The fix is to add `<WarnOnPackingNonPackableProject>false</WarnOnPackingNonPackableProject>` explicitly in the project file.

Aside from that, the lines:

```xml
<Nullable>enable</Nullable>
<ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>
```

should not appear in individual project files, because they are globally defined in `shared.props`. But after importing `shared.props`, a new warning appears:
```
CS7022: The entry point of the program is global code; ignoring 'Program.Main(string[])' entry point
```

This is because the project name ends with ".Test", so `shared-test.props` gets imported, whose package references cause this error. One of them (likely `Microsoft.AspNetCore.TestHost`) produces a `Program` class to make a .dll file runnable. The fix is to rename the Razor Pages project.

Additionally, all .slnf files were regenerated to match up with the latest cross-dependencies in projects.

Fixes #1485, fixes #1472.
